_comment: Bleakhold Royale v2 terrain, 'Sunglass Lagoon' (royale-spec.md sections 2, 3.3-3.6, 6.6): the same 3x3-tile
solo battle royale as v1 (map 901 BleakholdRoyale, zone 5100, subzones 5101-5113, battleground 12), rebuilt
as a bright tropical island valley. World X is north, Y is west; the block spans X and Y -1066.67..533.33,
centre C (-266.67, -266.67), written as an explicit 'centre' POI. The light is fixed at noon
(bleakhold_royale_v2.json: Map.dbc time 720, Light 1690 Sholazar, zone template 490 with Stranglethorn's
jungle ambience and music), so it is never dark.
Ring: a 'mountains' range 90 yd deep (peaks 125-205 above a 38 yd cliff, no ledges, seed 13) plus a steep
'border' band 58-100 yd in from the tile edge, so walkable ground stops 704 yd from C on either axis, inside
the server square (Bounds.HalfSize 750) and the pin area (C +- 730). No holes: players drop in anywhere.
Twenty-seven foothill spurs (24-28 deg, in groups with bays between) rise from 5-25 yd inside the foot
straight into the cliff; jungle moss greens the walls from z 52 (rock shows in streaks and on the sheerest
faces), vines hang on them, and big cliff rocks sit high on the range (z >= 75): mountains, not a wall. One
small stock-collision set piece stands in each bay before the walls, >= 80 yd from the foot: titan stones
(north), an ancestor gate (east), a serpent shrine (south) and eagle steps (west).
Centre (ring A): the turquoise Sunglass Lagoon (level 7; a 70 yd shelf leaves a wadeable band 0.7-1.5 yd
deep along every shore) with Sunstair Isle (5101, z 12) and its climbable ziggurat on a weathered square
plaza, ringed by a sand apron at z 8 that bulges west-south-west, opens a bay east-south-east and trails a
dry spit toward Gull Rock, and reached over four curved
wading sandbars (0.7 yd deep, 11-14 yd wide; the north one is the Tidewalk crossing, 5114). Palm Key (two
lobes) and Gull Rock (three lobes) sit in the lagoon with five sea stacks: rock cones steeper than 56 deg
centred on height-grid vertices, so no face or top is a landing spot. Ring C, where the storm ends: Tidecall
Village (5102, troll huts and a pier on the north bay), Kingfisher Point (5107, the watchtower hill), Sunbloom
Meadow (5106, blossom and a giant canopy tree), Totem Knoll (5116), Heron Rise (5117), Mossvine Hollow (5108,
giant trees and stilt huts), Bamboo Reach (5109), Saltwreck Cove (5104, the beached wreck) and Salvagers'
Camp (5115). Ring B, early game only: Twinfall Terrace (5103, z 34, the tarn and twin falls, north-east),
Serpent Steps (5105, z 30, temple ruins, south-west) and Sunwatch Falls (5110, z 22, below the lobby); their
valley edges are escarpments with smooth lips (two sine waves of 160 and 70 yd, up to 17 yd in and out, still
at the falls, ramps, river exits and nearby POIs) and a few rocks along them. Low rises
roll the open fields. The lobby, Sunwatch Overlook (5113), is a balcony at z 44.7 notched into the north-west
peaks; a steep cone skirt keeps walkable ground 54 yd from (455, 455); a BG collision ring stands on its rim.
Water (LiquidType 1 only; lakes and rivers carve their own beds, before the mountains): the lagoon and four
irregular mountain pools (Mirror Tarn, Serpent Pool, Sunwatch Pool, Mossvine Pool), and four meandering rivers
1.0-1.1 yd deep (waded anywhere; a vertex every ~22 yd, a bend every 70-90 yd) that fall from the terraces:
Twinfall East and its narrower tributary Twinfall West (two 25 yd falls), Serpent (through a ravine with two
rope bridges, the Vine Bridge crossing 5112) and Sunwatch (the 11 yd shelf fall seen from the lobby). Stepping
Stones (5111) is the ford on the Twinfall river. Four tall decorative falls drop from the ring into the pools.
Textures: 9 entries, at most 4 per chunk (grass, path, rock and moss everywhere; sand and bed on the shores;
one accent per region: flowers, jungle or temple tiles). Grass, flowers and jungle carry ground clutter
(GroundEffectTexture 22767, 4690, 671). Beaches paint the lagoon's shores (18 yd, a strong edge noise, so
sandy coves alternate with grassy banks); river banks and the pools stay grass and rock over the pale bed
(sand only at the river mouths); no wet sand.
'pois' feed the server's bh_royale_poi table (package.py poi-sql): 1 lobby, 13 landmarks and 3 crossings
(ids = area ids), the centre, 9 final sites (weights, all within 490 yd of C, each dry for 45 yd with stock
collision cover), 2 Shadow Sight orbs, 8 buff orbs (param 1 speed x3, 2 restoration x2, 3 berserk x3),
16 supply sites, 58 common crates (Crates.Max is 44) and 6 strongboxes. Every landmark, crate, orb and site
stands on terrain outside every WMO box; only the Vine Bridge crossing takes its z from a WMO (z_from). A
player without a pin (or sent back inside the square) lands on a landmark's highest surface, so landmarks
stand on open flat ground beside their buildings, never on a roof, the ziggurat or the fountain.
Art mixes Classic, TBC and WotLK stock models with later-expansion assets written as {modern, fallback,
kind}; offline (no --resolution) every one uses its 3.3.5a fallback. Modern doodads are client-only
decoration (no server collision or line of sight), so all collidable cover is stock, and modern trees stand
only in the unreachable mountain band. Palms clump along the lagoon's shores and at the river mouths, groves
of stock palms and jungle trees and stands of meadow trees fill the open fields, the jungle grows dense with
clearings, ferns line the river banks. No modern M2 names its files by FileDataID except the Zandalari props
and the shore kelp, which have no loadable equivalent in the kit and always fall back.
Every base path is in the asset kit v2 (kit_v2.json); every WMO carries the kit's measured box ('bounds').
The giant bat totem and the crest tree are backdrops outside the square.
